name: PID_Line_Tracer_V2
description: Improved dual-color-sensor PID line tracer using standard SPIKE-RT v0.2.0 APIs only. Startup mode menu: LEFT selects line tracing, RIGHT selects calibration, CENTER confirms. Calibration drives straight across a transverse black line from white to black to white and independently calibrates sensors B/F. Line tracing classifies centered, left-edge, right-edge, both-dark/crossing, and transition states. It also computes relative differential-drive wheel odometry (X/Y, heading, distance, speed, yaw rate, curvature) from A/E encoders using 88 mm wheels and 144 mm track, and uses measured yaw rate for conservative damping and speed adaptation. Includes a 10 ms cyclic notification, measured control interval, filtered derivative, conditional integral anti-windup, adaptive speed, and force sensor C start/stop. No driver modifications. The built-in SPIKE Prime LSM6DS3TR-C IMU is initialized using the standard hub_imu API. A stationary 3-axis gyro bias/noise estimate is recorded; when Z-axis calibration quality passes thresholds, 85% bias-corrected gyro yaw and 15% encoder yaw are fused for heading, motion classification, speed adaptation, steering damping, and X/Y odometry. The 3-axis acceleration/angular velocity, both yaw estimates, their disagreement, fused pose, line state, and motor commands are logged at 5 Hz. If gyro calibration quality is poor or IMU initialization fails, encoder-only odometry remains active. No driver modifications. While line tracing is in standby (before force-sensor start), the program also emits a 5 Hz idle IMU/encoder yaw record without commanding the motors, allowing stationary-noise and hand-rotation sign checks.
warning: Calibration requires both color sensors to start on white, with the robot facing straight toward a black line that crosses the direction of travel. Keep the robot unobstructed during calibration. Odometry is relative and will drift with wheel slip or incorrect wheel geometry; it cannot identify absolute line position when both sensors see equal white. Verify wheel diameter/track width, motor direction, calibration thresholds, control timing, and PID/odometry gains on the actual robot. Keep the robot completely stationary during the approximately 1 second gyro-bias calibration. Keep the robot stationary during the approximately 1 second gyro-bias calibration. IMU fusion starts only if Z-axis bias/noise checks pass; otherwise encoder-only yaw is used. The initial gyro/encoder blend is 85/15 and must be validated on the real robot before treating it as tuned. Before pressing force sensor C, use the idle log to check stationary gyro Z and gently rotate the robot by hand to verify the yaw sign. Do not start line tracing until the sign and calibration behavior are understood.
